subject: Security exhibit & audit rights — pen test windows / evidence cadence
messages:
From: Mike Rao <mike.rao@healthsync.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@healthsync.com
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit language — pen test access and evidence cadence

Marissa,

Thanks for taking the call last week. Legal at HealthSync is working through the MSA and we want to confirm a few items in the security exhibit before we proceed to signature:

- Penetration testing access: we need clarity on notice period and a rolling 30- to 60-day window where tests can be scheduled.
- Evidence cadence: our auditors ask for at least monthly artifact snapshots for SOC 2 assertions during onboarding and quarterly thereafter.
- Data access during audits: confirmation on whether live production access is required or whether scoped read-only exports suffice.

Can Redwood confirm the proposed language (or offer alternate text) so we can avoid back-and-forth with procurement? If you can loop in your security/assurance lead and legal, that would help.

Attached is our internal vendor intake (redacted).

—Mike Rao
General Counsel, HealthSync Therapeutics
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Rao <mike.rao@healthsync.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language — pen test access and evidence cadence

Mike — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Jonas (legal) and Ben (security ops) to propose concise redlines.

Quick answers up front:
- Pen test window: Redwood can offer a 30-day rolling notice window for non-emergency tests and a 7-day notice option for scheduled maintenance/approved test partners. We typically avoid on-demand live exploitation without prior coordination.
- Evidence cadence: we can provide monthly snapshot artifacts (logs/configs) during onboarding for up to 3 months, then quarterly snapshots aligned with SOC 2 reporting. If you need longer retention for procurement reasons, we can add a 6-month retention addendum.
- Audit access: scoped, read-only exports (S3-signed links + CSV/JSON extracts) are our standard for customer evidence delivery; privileged live access requires a separate privileged-inspection process and an inspection SLA.

I attached our last SOC 2 summary and a draft redline doc for the MSA exhibit. Jonas — can you review the proposed phrasing in the attached doc and suggest a short alternative for their procurement team? Ben — ping on operational constraints (blackout windows, staging for pen tests).

Next step: Jonas to provide suggested redline text today; I’ll coordinate a 30-min call with HealthSync if they want to walk the language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mike Rao <mike.rao@healthsync.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language — pen test access and evidence cadence

Mike / Marissa — reviewed and drafted a compact set of redlines below that should map cleanly into the MSA/Order Form security exhibit. Keeping language short to minimize procurement churn.

1) Penetration testing / security assessments
- Redwood will permit vendor-initiated penetration tests on a rolling 30-day notice basis. For critical/infra-impacting tests Redwood and the customer will mutually agree to a 7-day scheduled window.
- All penetration tests must be coordinated with Redwood’s security operations (security-ops@redwood.ai). Redwood reserves the right to require a staging test environment for high-impact scenarios.

2) Audit rights and evidence delivery
- For SOC 2 and related attestations, Redwood will provide read-only artifact exports (logs, configuration snapshots, control evidence) via temporary signed links within 7 business days of a written request.
- During onboarding Redwood will provide monthly evidence snapshots for the first 90 days; thereafter evidence will be provided quarterly unless otherwise agreed in writing.

3) Scope and limitations
- Audit access is limited to the customer’s instance/tenant and excludes cross-tenant production data. Live interactive sessions requiring privileged access will be provided only under an agreed inspection process and with a named Redwood contact.
- Redwood will not permit unscoped live exploitation of production systems; coordinated, scoped tests in staging are preferred.

4) Remediation & SLAs
- Redwood will acknowledge security findings within 3 business days and provide an initial remediation plan within 10 business days. Critical findings will be treated as priority and Redwood will propose mitigations within an agreed escalation cadence.

I attached a tracked-change doc with these redlines. Marissa — if HealthSync can accept this scope we can bake it into the Order Form and attach the SOC2 summary as an evidentiary artifact. Mike — flagged two choices for you: (A) accept the monthly->quarterly cadence with staging carveouts, or (B) request extended onboarding cadence (monthly for 6 months). Which does procurement prefer?

—Jonas Weber
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Mike Rao <mike.rao@healthsync.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language — pen test access and evidence cadence

Jonas/Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. Procurement reviewed option A and prefers the monthly->quarterly cadence but requests explicit language that Redwood will provide a named Redwood point of contact for any live inspection requests and a calendar link for available pen test windows (the calendar .ics you attached looks like a good start).

We also asked for the 3-business-day acknowledgement and 10-business-day initial remediation plan to be added to the exhibit as a commitment (noted). For our internal risk committee, can Redwood confirm the SOC 2 summary includes CC6 and CC7 mappings (redacted ok)? If yes we’ll move to signature and route the Order Form to DocuSign.

Assuming you confirm CC6/CC7 mapping language, procurement will execute next week.

—Mike
General Counsel, HealthSync Therapeutics
